findings.quote: she preserved toward all of them without surpassing measure the same goodwill and motherly affection down to the end of her life
findings.problem: Greek: πρὸς πάντας τούτους ἀνυπέρβλητον διεφύλαξε τὴν εὔνοιαν καὶ φιλοστοργίαν. ἀνυπέρβλητον means 'unsurpassable/unsurpassed'; 'without surpassing measure' reads as 'without excess' (inverts the sense), and 'the same' has no Greek counterpart.
findings.proposed_fix: she preserved toward all of them unsurpassed goodwill and motherly affection down to the end of her life

findings.quote: Ostiagon the Galatian, king of the Galatians in Asia
findings.problem: Greek: Ὀρτιάγων ὁ Γαλάτης. The name is Ortiagon (so also in Book 21, 'Chiomara, the wife of Ortiagon'); 'Ostiagon' is a misrendering and breaks identity with the Book 21 figure. The chapter heading carries the same form.
findings.proposed_fix: Ortiagon the Galatian, king of the Galatians in Asia

units.note: The heading 'Ostiagon Tries to Become King of All the Galatians' should also read Ortiagon (outside the quote scope).
